turns.text: Certus safety hotline. I'm recording a safety report. Which system is this about?
Hi, this is Captain Dana Reyes, I fly the 737 on the line. I want to report a problem with the Boeing flight controls.
Captain Reyes, thank you for calling. I'm recording your report on Boeing Flight Controls. What happened?

On approach this morning we flew through a gusty crosswind with some sideslip. The two angle of attack vanes disagreed by about five degrees and we got the AOA DISAGREE alert, but the stall protection never moved the trim. We got the stick shaker close to the stall, I recovered by hand and we lost about five hundred feet.
Understood, Captain. When did this happen—what date and time, or what phase of flight?
Around seven forty this morning, on the approach into Denver. I'd call it hazardous. Nobody was hurt.
Thank you. What was your aircraft type, weight and center of gravity, and what other alerts did you see besides the AOA DISAGREE?
It was a 737-800, about 66 tonnes with an aft CG, flaps up, thrust at idle, and the autopilot was off.

I have your report, Captain Reyes. Let me read back what you've told me: On approach into Denver at 0740 this morning, a 737-800 at 66 tonnes with aft CG experienced an AOA DISAGREE alert in gusty crosswind conditions with sideslip, the stall protection trim did not move, stick shaker activated near stall, and you recovered by hand losing 500 feet. You rate this hazardous with no injuries. Is that correct?
Yes, that's correct. Please file it.
